SI-4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: ABIDE (I+II): Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I and II combined; HBN: Healthy Brain Network at Child Mind Institute; ADHD-200: ADHD-200 Consortium; femaleASD: Multimodal Developmental Neurogenetics of Females with ASD from NIMH NDAR; SINGLE-SITE includes POND (Province of Ontario Neurodevelopmental Network), UK MRC-AIMS (Cambridge site), and UCSD Biomarkers of Autism study; None (Pre-Trained NM): BrainCharts reference model based on 75,241 TD individuals was used as the pre-trained normative model for generating centile scores
DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "T1-weighted scans were combined from 49 sites across 7 datasets, including the ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange), the POND (Province of Ontario Neurodevelopmental) Network, the HBN (Healthy Brain Network) at the Child Mind Institute, the ADHD200 Consortium, the Multimodal Developmental Neurogenetics of Females with ASD dataset from the National Institute of Mental Health Data Archive, the UK MRC-AIMS (Medical Research Council Autism Imaging Multi-centre Study), and the University of California San Diego Biomarkers of Autism study." ... "Our previous work generated reference models using generalized additive models of location scale and shape to map neuroanatomical developmental trajectories across the life span, using a sample of 75,241 TD individuals"
DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Bedford2025.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Sample and Datasets, L41-43; L55-56

answer.ABIDE (I+II): clinical sample source (autism and TD controls)

answer.HBN: clinical sample source (autism, ADHD, and TD controls)

answer.ADHD-200: clinical sample source (ADHD and TD controls)

answer.femaleASD: clinical sample source (autism and TD controls, female-enriched)

answer.POND: clinical sample source (autism, ADHD, and TD controls)

answer.UK MRC-AIMS: clinical sample source (autism and TD controls, Cambridge site only)

answer.UCSD: clinical sample source (autism and TD controls, infant/toddler sample)

answer.BrainCharts (Pre-Trained NM): reference normative model for generating out-of-sample centile scores (75,241 TD individuals)

DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The seven datasets (ABIDE, POND, HBN, ADHD200, femaleASD, UK-AIMS, UCSD) provided clinical samples for applying the normative model to characterize autism and ADHD. The BrainCharts reference model (based on 75,241 TD individuals from 100 studies) served as the pre-trained normative model to generate centile scores benchmarking each participant against typical brain development trajectories.
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Here, we leveraged models of average brain development previously characterized by our group to quantify alterations related to autism and ADHD." ... "Out-of-sample centile scores for our study sample were generated based on these reference models using Brent's maximum likelihood estimation." ... "Centile scores quantify variation in brain development and range from 0 to 1, with 0.5 representing the average of the reference sample."
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Bedford2025.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Sample and Datasets, L41-44; Generation of Centile Scores, L53-61

answer.note: The study used a pre-trained normative model from BrainCharts (Bethlehem et al., 2022) based on 75,241 TD individuals. The current study sample included 1,869 TD controls (post-QC) which were used for out-of-sample centile estimation but not for training the normative model itself.

DC-3_healthy_control_n_of_each_normative.detail: The normative model was pre-trained externally using BrainCharts data. The 75,241 TD individuals were used to establish the reference trajectories. In the current study, 1,869 TD controls (post-QC) from the 7 combined datasets were included for applying the out-of-sample centile estimation, not for model training.

answer.note: The BrainCharts reference model (75,241 TD) age statistics are not reported in this paper. For the current study sample (all groups combined, N=4255 post-QC): ages 2-64 years, mean 14.0, median 12.4. TD-specific age: mean 15.0, sd 7.9 (from Table S1.2.5).

DC-4_age_info_of_each_normative_model.detail: Age information for the pre-trained BrainCharts normative model (75,241 TD) is not provided in this paper; it is referenced to Bethlehem et al. 2022. The current study sample age range is 2-64 years with mean 14.0 and median 12.4. TD controls in this study: mean age 15.0 (sd 7.9).
